RESOLUTION -Authorizing an independent professional traffic safety planning study be
conducted for the intersection of Pershing Boulevard and Duff Avenue in the City of Cheyenne,
Wyoming.Tom Mason, Director, Metropolitan Planning Organization(MPO), recommended the study
be facilitated through the MPO, explaining that assignment to the MPO would provide for a more
detailed and indepth study involving other neighborhood and community elements, and public
involvement.He provided information on the MPO'sfederal funding cycle and the MPO Policy
Committee's involvement in approving projects; expressed his belief that timing of the study is
2:
important relativeto current area construction that could affect accuracy of results, and recommended
developing the scope of work to be included in the study be done in the summer with hiring of a
consultant toconduct the study later to coincide with theM PO budget cycle, contingent upon the Policy
Committee's approval, and when construction has been completed in the area. Upon inquiry, Mr.
Mason provided information on agrant theM PO received last summer to develop acomplete streets
policy, which could be included in Plan Cheyenne, and noted the policy would address transportation
routes for cars, pedestrians and bicyclists.Anne Picot, member, Mayor's Council for People with
Disabilities, commented on pedestrian safety concerns at the Pershing/Duff intersection and expressed
concerns with postponing the study, stating timely resolution to the issue should be achieved.Lee Filer,
Crisp, chairman, Mayor's Council for People with Disabilities, advised the Council does not support
the resolution in its current state but would support a study by MPO with a complete street policy that
would encompass traffic, pedestrians, and businesses located near the intersection.Debbie Mass en gill,

crossing.Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr.Brown stated there was no recommendation on the

Under other business:
Pete Laybourn thanked Council members for supporting the traffic studyto be conducted at the
intersection of Pershing Blvd.and Duff Avenue.Heexpressed concerns with the“failure”of concrete
at the intersection as well as other locations within the City, and requested Council members be diligent
in having good quality concrete for street, curb and gutter projects.
Lee Filer, state legislative representative, expressed concerns on the following issues: Repair
costs of a sewer line incurred by a constituent and City vs. homeowner's area of responsibility;
sanitation fee assessments involving 40 tenants in the Majestic apartment building; mandatory
residential recycling bin fee; deterioration of curbs, gutters and sidewalks in certain neighborhoods,
development, licensing and inspections, and need forflashing lights and crosswalks, in addition to
current signage, near certain elementary schools for student crossing safety.During queries raised by
Representative Filer throughout his statements, Mayor Kaysen offered tomeet withthe constituent and
Acting City Engineer, provided information available involving the topics of sanitation and recyling
fees, and schedule of certain street repairs/renovation projects. Comments made by some Council
members regarded a suggested area that should be reviewed for street repairs or reconstruction and
flashing lights/crosswalk designations atcertain schools; residential responsibility involving sewer lines,
andlevel of state funding assistance to municipalities.
